Items GUI-002, GUI-003, GUI-004, GUI-005, GUI-006, GUI-007, GUI-008, GUI-009, GUI-010, GUI-011, GUI-012, GUI-013, GUI-014 remain proposed because their existing acceptance gates are not satisfied by the current source changes alone.

items.title: Design a target-bound regional quota preflight for deployments
items.problem: The Maester preprovision hook warns from the count of regional Automation Accounts, but a count cannot show the subscription's effective per-region limit or remaining capacity. azd-gui has no authoritative capacity result before a deployment action allowed by the active project contract, so ARM can still reject account creation after preparation.
scope: Investigate supported read-only data sources for Automation Account usage and quota by subscription and region, including their permission and provider prerequisites. Microsoft's documented portal flow shows regional Automation Account usage and limits; the Quota REST API's documented provider set does not include Automation and its prerequisites include Microsoft.Quota registration and Quota Request Operator. The stable Automation ARM spec version 2024-10-23 defines account listing and an account-scoped Usages route, but no subscription/region account-quota operation; confirm whether any other supported endpoint can answer the pre-create question.
Design a native, host-owned capacity-check contract bound to the exact cloud, subscription, region, resource type, source and check time; do not accept arbitrary template scripts or URLs.

Specify clear pre-deployment behavior for available, exhausted, unknown, stale, forbidden, timed-out, cancelled and retried checks, including plain-language next steps and invalidation when the bound target or configuration changes.
Respect the active project contract: do not add or restore a blocked deployment route, copyable reviewed command, arbitrary command, or terminal handoff as part of quota discovery.
Keep the first supported use case to Azure Automation Account regional quota; do not imply that other resource types or all Azure capacity are covered.
acceptance: Document whether a supported read-only API exposes Automation Account per-region usage and limit; identify exact permissions and provider-registration requirements, and distinguish a portal view from a programmatic API.
Define target-bound available, exhausted and unknown results with evidence source and check time; existing-account counts and saved reports are not authoritative quota proof.

For each deployment action already allowed by the active project contract, confirmed exhaustion blocks that action; unavailable or stale data remains visibly unknown and points to the documented manual quota view. Any override must be a separate explicit acknowledgement bound to the current check. This discovery must not create a deployment path, terminal handoff, or copyable reviewed command where the project contract blocks one.

Keep quota reads read-only. Do not register providers, request quota changes, add scopes/consent, switch target, or deploy as part of this discovery. Record that a quota result is not a capacity reservation and ARM may still reject a later create.
Define deterministic fixtures for sufficient, exhausted, unsupported/unknown, permission denied, stale target, timeout, cancellation and retry; no live tenant mutation.
validation: Review Microsoft Learn documentation for Azure Automation quotas, Azure Quota REST provider support, and the Azure portal Quotas view; inspect the stable Automation ARM specification and record API version, permissions and limitations.
Review current native permission-preflight and terminal-handoff contracts before selecting the host-owned integration point.
Use deterministic fixtures for every documented result and invalidation case; keep live quota requests, quota increases and deployment outside the item.
Validate docs/backlog.json and regenerate/check docs/backlog.md with the checked azd-reference backlog tooling.
evidence: Reviewed current Microsoft Automation, Azure Quota, and Azure Support documentation and the stable Automation ARM 2024-10-23 specification against main cf221d0f95efd3c055940f2a68642c8e9e6ec861. The portal exposes the manual subscription and region view. The reviewed APIs offer no supported pre-create quota and usage read.

docs/automation-regional-quota.md records the operator path, host-owned target binding, and deterministic acceptance cases for a future supported API. Runtime automation requires new provider evidence. No Azure requests or permission changes were required for discovery.
